subject: Melrose Residential Heat Pump Program Presentation
overview: The committee received a detailed presentation from Melrose Sustainability Manager Martha Grover regarding community heat pump adoption and municipal electrification programs. Members also finalized logistics for upcoming community events and reviewed city-wide sustainability initiatives.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from the May 1 meeting.

items.title: Administrative Updates
items.summary: Alicia Hunt reported on new department staffing, summer interns, and the ongoing review of proposals for the city's waste and recycling contract.

items.title: Circle the Square Planning
items.summary: Members discussed logistics for the June 17 festival, including staffing a table with materials on invasive plants, native pollinators, and Mass Save rebates.

items.title: Rodent Control Education
items.summary: The committee reviewed an educational video regarding rodent behavior and discussed the potential use of rodent birth control to reduce reliance on harmful rodenticides.

items.title: Harvest Energy Festival
items.summary: Planning for the October 14 event included confirming food vendors, a beer garden, and logistics for on-site paper shredding and electronics recycling.

items.title: Melrose Heat Pump Program Presentation
items.summary: Martha Grover detailed Melrose's use of the Mass Save Community First Partnership to fund heat pump 'coaches' and third-party advisors who help residents navigate complex installations. She also demonstrated the 'Block Maps' tool used to target outreach to residents using oil or electric resistance heating.

items.title: Trees Medford and Reforestation Bill
items.summary: The committee reviewed a state legislative bill aimed at establishing a Municipal Reforestation Program and discussed the city's need for volunteer ambassadors to water young trees.

items.title: Herbicide and Pollinator Updates
items.summary: Members discussed the health risks of Roundup and proposed creating educational flyers about alternative weed control methods, while noting an upcoming pollinator garden project at City Hall.

items.title: Scheduling and Adjournment
items.summary: The committee discussed potential July dates for an in-person summer meeting and potluck.
